name: flow_reader
description: Read an nfcapd flow file (nfdump's own file of decoded NetFlow v5, NetFlow v9 or IPFIX records) with the pinned nfdump, as a reader: it runs nfdump -V, -v, -I, -E and -o json, never nfcapd or nfpcapd, and nothing here listens on a port. Supported input: an nfcapd file (uncompressed, or compressed by nfdump; the layout version and compression are read from nfdump -v and reported). Refused by name before any program runs: a capture (pcap or pcapng; no mode of the pinned nfdump turns the export packets inside a capture into records, and nfpcapd builds new flows from the packets, which are not the exporter's records), sFlow (the pinned package ships nfcapd and nfpcapd only; its nfcapd does not decode sFlow and sfcapd is not installed), and any file that does not start with the nfcapd magic: a layout is not guessed from a sample. declared_format is required and says what the dataset is said to be (netflow_v5, netflow_v9, ipfix, sflow, nfcapd); for the three export protocols the exporters the file lists must all be of that protocol or the answer is partial. Per file the answer gives the file's size and SHA-256, nfdump's verification, its own statistics (flows, packets and bytes by protocol, first and last second, sequence failures, the collector's ident string), and the exporters nfdump lists: the UDP address the collector saw, the protocol, the observation domain or source id (for NetFlow v5 the engine type and id), sequence failures, export packets, flows and any sampler the exporter announced. Each record is a row with its source file, its position in nfdump's output (the locator) and the parser; the times nfdump printed (run with TZ=UTC, so UTC, with fractions of a second, beside the raw text and an epoch in milliseconds) and the collector's receive time, which is not the exporter's clock; protocol, addresses, ports and TCP flags; counters with a flag saying whether nfdump marked the record sampled; the direction nfdump stored; the translated (post-NAT) fields nfdump names xlt; interfaces and ToS; the exporter that sent it; and every other field nfdump printed under extra. SAMPLING: a record nfdump marked sampled has counters nfdump scaled by the announced sampling (observed for a NetFlow v5 header interval): an estimate, and counters_exact is false for it; a record that is not marked is not shown to be unsampled (nfdump marks only the sampling it understood), so counters_exact is null for it and never true; the totals keep the two apart. NOT PROVIDED (stated in every answer): template ids and templates (an nfcapd file keeps decoded records), the exporter's active and inactive timeouts, whether a record is one direction or both, a byte offset of a record, and the export packets. nfdump's exit codes are not trusted (it exits 0 on a file it could not read): nfdump -v, -I, -E and -o json are all run, any message on stderr, any output line the parsers do not know, a nonzero exit, and a record count that differs from the file's own flow count make the file partial, or failed when no record was read; a file whose bytes were changed inside a record that still decodes is not detected (compare the SHA-256). The rows are paged: the first limit are answered inline and the whole list is the JSON Lines file all_results names, placed without replacing an earlier one; nfdump's own messages for each file are kept beside it. max_records (default 100000, at most 500000) bounds the records read from one file; a file with more is read up to the bound, the answer is partial and says so. The tool's own clock (max_seconds, default 900, at most 1000) is below the manifest's timeout and covers hashing, every nfdump run and the parsing; a program still running at the end is killed with everything it started. Programs run in the tool's own process group (never a session of its own) with the kernel asked to end them if the tool dies. The input is opened for reading only. The answer is addresses, ports, counters and times, no payload; the ident string is text from the file and is shown as it is. A volume is a bound with its sampling, never a measured total, and a flow record is not a connection and shows nothing of content or intent. A process nfdump leaves behind after it exits (a child that holds its stdout or stderr, which are files here, in the tool's process group or in a session of its own, or one that holds no descriptor) is stopped, killed and reaped by the shared process block's settle() before the records and messages are read; one found, or a host where the absence of one cannot be proven (not Linux, PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER refused), makes the answer at most partial (program_group.left_behind, program_group.unproven and a line under problems), and the files nfdump wrote are then what the leftover had written when it was ended. A process that is no descendant of nfdump (started through a service manager) is not found.

inputs.description: The nfcapd files to read (1 to 32, each a regular file, never written). A capture, an sFlow dataset or any file without the nfcapd magic is refused by name

declared_format.description: Required: what the dataset is said to be: netflow_v5, netflow_v9, ipfix, sflow or nfcapd (an nfcapd file of mixed or unstated protocol). sflow is refused; for the three export protocols the exporters the file lists are checked against it

limit.description: Record rows answered inline (default 200); the whole list is the file all_results names

max_records.description: The most records read from one file (default 100000, 1 to 500000). A file with more is read up to it and the answer is partial

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock, 10 to 1000 seconds, default 900, over hashing, every nfdump run and the parsing: a program still running at the end is killed with everything it started
